record.summary: Government response to the consultation on the March 2023 AI regulation white paper. It keeps the five cross-sectoral principles for existing regulators on a non-statutory basis, sets up a central function in DSIT for cross-sectoral AI risk monitoring and regulator coordination, and plans targeted consultation on a cross-economy AI risk register. For highly capable general-purpose AI it relies for now on voluntary measures by developers and on testing of models before and after deployment, led by the AI Safety Institute, and sets out the case for future targeted binding requirements on their developers.
record.notes: Presented to Parliament on 6 February 2024 as Command Paper CP 1019, in response to the consultation on the white paper of March 2023, which ran from 29 March to 21 June 2023 and received 409 responses. It asked a number of regulators to publish their strategic approach to AI by 30 April 2024, announced £10 million for regulators' AI capabilities and a steering committee of government and regulator representatives, and left a statutory duty on regulators to have due regard to the principles for after a review of an initial period of non-statutory implementation.

verification.note: Stored and read in this run: the GOV.UK consultation outcome page with the full text of the response (snapshot of 11 Oct 2026, unchanged on 17 Oct), which gives the title, CP 1019, presentation to Parliament on 6 February 2024 and the passages behind the summary and notes; and the consultation page (stored 17 Oct 2026 and proposed as the new secondary source), which records 'Government response to consultation published' on 6 February 2024, the consultation period and 409 responses, with the response's web-ready and print-ready PDFs. The former secondary source was the white paper's publication page (GB-01's source), and the two PDFs linked from the response page are a November 2023 response to a different review and the white paper's March 2023 impact assessment. Version 1's notes on the Labour government's plans for frontier-AI legislation are not in a stored file and were removed (see open questions).

summary.quote: In March 2023, we published our AI regulation white paper
The proposed framework outlined five cross-sectoral principles for the UK’s existing regulators to interpret and apply within their remits.
We have recruited a new multidisciplinary team to undertake cross-sectoral risk monitoring within the Department for Science, Innovation and Technology (DSIT)
We have already started developing the central function to support effective risk monitoring, regulator coordination, and knowledge exchange.
We will conduct targeted consultations on our cross-economy AI risk register
both before and after models are deployed. In the UK, the newly established AI Safety Institute (see Box 4) leads this work.
Here we lay out a pro-innovation case for further targeted binding requirements on the small number of organisations developing highly capable general-purpose AI systems

notes.quote: We are asking a number of regulators to publish an update outlining their strategic approach to AI by 30 April 2024.
£10 million to jumpstart regulator’s AI capabilities
including a new steering committee with government and regulator representatives
we anticipate introducing a statutory duty on regulators requiring them to have due regard to the principles after reviewing an initial period of non-statutory implementation
This consultation ran from 11am on 29 March 2023 to 11:45pm on 21 June 2023
We received 409 responses to this consultation from a wide range of stakeholders

judgment.status_reasoning: A non-binding consultation response presented to Parliament on 6 February 2024; the response page and the consultation page (stored 17 Oct 2026) show no withdrawal and no update after that day, and GOV.UK marks both as published under the 2022 to 2024 Sunak government. 'Published (non-binding, current)' stands; whether a later government statement replaced it is not in a stored file (open question).
judgment.scope_reasoning: UK government framework for AI regulation with frontier-AI safety content; in scope with no note.

extra_urls.reason: The consultation page that the stored response names as its parent (breadcrumb link): it lists the outcome with its publication date and any later updates, and is proposed as the record's secondary_url in place of the white paper's own page.

open_questions: Version 1's notes said that the Labour government elected in July 2024 signalled targeted frontier-AI legislation, that no government AI bill had been introduced as of October 2026 and that reports in 2025 said it had been deferred. No stored file supports these statements, so they were removed. Whether a later government statement or bill has replaced this response's approach needs an official source.
